title: Add rate limiting to the API
subtitle: feature/rate-limit → main · 5 files

steps.title: Rename the auth middleware to guards
summary: The middleware now does more than authentication, so it moves to guards.ts.
This step is the move only — the behaviour change comes next — so the rename reads as a clean structural step.

files.note: Pure move — no content change here. The logic edits are shown in the next step.

steps.title: Tighten the guard check
steps.summary: Inside the moved file, the guard becomes stricter — kept separate from the rename so the real behaviour change stands on its own.

note: checkAuth gains a strict mode: when on, it requires a longer token (length > 3) instead of just non-empty.
requireUser now opts into strict mode, so unauthenticated requests are rejected more aggressively.
MODULE_NAME updated to "guards" to match the new filename.

steps.title: Add the token-bucket rate limiter
steps.summary: A new RateLimiter implementing a token-bucket algorithm, exposed as Express middleware.

note: New RateLimiter class with configurable capacity and refill-per-second.
Per-key token buckets refill continuously based on elapsed time.
Exposes middleware() that returns a 429 with a Retry-After header when a bucket is empty.

steps.title: Wire the limiter into the app
steps.summary: Register the limiter ahead of the guards, and give the 429 path a typed error.

note: Instantiate RateLimiter(120, 2) and mount its middleware before requireUser.
Import path updated to the renamed ./middleware/guards module.

files.note: Add RateLimitError extending HttpError, so the 429 response has a typed error to throw.

steps.title: Cover the limiter with a test
steps.summary: A first test asserting the middleware shape; the bucket-math harness follows in a later PR.

files.note: Smoke test that RateLimiter.middleware() returns a function — a placeholder until the timing-based tests land.
